Direct dependency of def-relu-network; current supplier carrier items/def-feedforward-neural-network.md has status draft. Exact supplier excerpt: Fix integers $d,r\ge1$. A finite feedforward computation graph from $\mathbb R^d$ to $\mathbb R^r$ consists of a finite directed graph $(V,E)$ with no directed cycle; pairwise disjoint input, hidden, and output vertex sets $I,H,O$ whose union is $V$; exactly $d$ input vertices and $r$ output vertices; and a specified ordering of $V$ in which the tail of every directed edge precedes its head. The input vertices are labelled bijectively by the coordinates $1,\ldots,d$, and input vertex $i$ has value $x_i$ for $x\in\mathbb R^d$. Each non-input vertex $v$ has a real bias $b_v$, a real weight $w_{uv}$ for every edge $u\to v$, and a real activation function $\rho_v$. Direct dependency of lem-sobolev-taylor-grid-approximation; current supplier carrier items/def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm.md has status published. Exact supplier excerpt: For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition. Current use: The Taylor-grid lemma and its consumers use the weak-derivative classes and the maximum norm when p=∞. The relevant supplier statement and complete proof where applicable were inspected; this records interface evidence, not independent approval.

Direct dependency of lem-sobolev-taylor-grid-approximation; current supplier carrier items/thm-w-one-infinity-functions-have-lipschitz-representatives.md has status published. Exact supplier excerpt: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge1$ and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, bounded and convex. If $u\in W^{1,\infty}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, then $u$ has a representative $u^{*}$ with
$$|u^{*}(x)-u^{*}(y)|\le\|Du\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\,|x-y|\qquad(x,y\in\Omega),$$
and $u^{*}=u$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. Conversely, every Lipschitz function $f:\Omega\to\mathbb K$ with constant $L$ lies in $W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)$ and $\|Df\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\le L$ for real scalars, while $\|Df\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\le\sqrt2 L$ for complex scalars. In both cases the real-linear derivative has operator norm at most $L$ almost everywhere. Current use: The grid lemma and adaptive theorem use the real-valued W1∞ representative and its gradient-controlled Lipschitz constant on the open convex cube or interval. The relevant supplier statement and complete proof where applicable were inspected; this records interface evidence, not independent approval.

Direct dependency of lem-sobolev-taylor-grid-approximation; current supplier carrier items/thm-local-smooth-approximation-in-wkp.md has status published. Exact supplier excerpt: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p<\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Fix a nonnegative
$\rho\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ of unit mass with
$\operatorname{supp}\rho\subseteq\overline B_1(0)$, put
$\rho_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon^{-n}\rho(x/\varepsilon)$, and define the
interior mollification
$$u_\varepsilon(x)=(\rho_\varepsilon*\widetilde u)(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\widetilde u(y)\,\rho_\varepsilon(x-y)\,dy,$$
where $\widetilde u$ is a representative of $u$ extended by zero to
$\mathbb R^n$. Then $u_\varepsilon\to u$ in $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every
open $U\subset\subset\Omega$; equivalently $u_\varepsilon\to u$ in
$W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. The exponent $p=1$ is included, and
no assertion about density or convergence in the $W^{k,\infty}$ norm is made. Current use: The Taylor-grid proof applies the local smoothing interface with k=n−1 and p=1 after converting bounded derivatives on the finite cube to W^{n−1,1}; it derives uniform convergence separately from the Lipschitz bound. The relevant supplier statement and complete proof where applicable were inspected; this records interface evidence, not independent approval.

Direct dependency of lem-sobolev-taylor-grid-approximation; current supplier carrier items/lem-mollification-commutes-with-weak-derivatives-in-the-interior.md has status published. Exact supplier excerpt: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$1\le p\le\infty$ and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$\rho\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ be nonnegative with
$\int_{\mathbb R^n}\rho=1$ and $\operatorname{supp}\rho\subseteq\overline B_1(0)$.
For $\varepsilon>0$ put $\rho_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon^{-n}\rho(x/\varepsilon)$
and
$$\Omega_\varepsilon=\{x\in\Omega:\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathbb R^n\setminus\Omega)>\varepsilon\},\qquad\Omega_\varepsilon=\mathbb R^n\ \text{when }\Omega=\mathbb R^n .$$
Then $\rho_\varepsilon*u$ is defined and smooth on $\Omega_\varepsilon$, and
for every multi-index $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le k$,
$$D^\alpha(\rho_\varepsilon*u)=\rho_\varepsilon*(D^\alpha u)\qquad\text{on }\Omega_\varepsilon,$$
as pointwise smooth functions for the constructed representatives and as
almost-everywhere classes. Here $D^\alpha u$ is extended by zero off $\Omega$
in the convolution. Current use: The Taylor-grid proof uses interior commutation for weak derivatives through order n, then bounds the convolution using its nonnegative unit-mass kernel. The relevant supplier statement and complete proof where applicable were inspected; this records interface evidence, not independent approval.
